hunt.justification: Business Email Compromise (BEC) resulting in fraudulent ACH transfers is a direct financial loss risk. Validating whether employees have successfully interacted with known lookalike domains confirms whether the current campaign has breached the human layer.

meta.name: Interaction with BEC Lookalike Infrastructure

related.reason: This hunt focuses on infrastructure interaction; another hunt is required to find internal persistence via email forwarding rules used to hide BEC replies.

meta.analysis: Simple detection rules alert on the domains themselves; this hunt links the DNS resolution lead to process-level socket state and HTTP URIs to determine if the social engineering was effective. The gated flow ensures that high-volume telemetry is only searched for specific high-fidelity leads.

coverage.reason: The dossier provides no hb_email surface or M365-native email logs to examine message headers, separators, or HTML comments.

scenario.summary: A large-scale business email compromise campaign used AI-assisted templates to impersonate company executives and vendor representatives to facilitate ACH payment fraud. The threat actor registered lookalike domains and used third-party email infrastructure to deliver over a million phishing emails containing fabricated invoices and simulated internal conversation threads.

meta.rationale: Prioritize finance and executive workstations as they are the intended targets of the ACH fraud lures. Use the hosts found in the dns-leads step to populate the scope_hosts parameter for the parallel connection investigation.
meta.hypothesis: An employee has received a BEC email and is interacting with lookalike infrastructure to view a fake invoice or initiate a fraudulent payment.

bec_domains.description: Known lookalike domains from the campaign report.

scope_hosts.description: Filter interaction queries to these hosts; leave empty to check the whole estate.

references.name: MSRC — Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud

blind_spots.risk: Modern browsers using DoH bypass traditional DNS resolvers, so the gate may close prematurely even if an interaction occurred.
blind_spots.question: whether the host used DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) to resolve lookalike domains

blind_spots.risk: If a target host lacks an agent, we see the connection at the network level but cannot attribute it to a specific user or application, leading to indeterminate verdicts.
blind_spots.question: which process initiated the connection to the fraud domains on unmanaged hosts

blind_spots.risk: We are hunting interactions without visibility into the delivery mechanism, missing the chance to see headers or AI markers in the source email.
blind_spots.question: whether the initial phishing email was successfully delivered and seen by the user

hunt.name: Interaction with BEC Lookalike Infrastructure
hunt.description: This hunt identifies internal interaction with infrastructure registered for AI-assisted executive impersonation. It uses a gated flow to first find low-cost DNS leads matching known lookalike patterns, then expands the investigation to process-level sockets and HTTP telemetry only when a lead is confirmed. The hunt distinguishes between simple email delivery and successful social engineering by verifying if an endpoint established a connection to the fraud domains.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, answers, COUNT(*) AS lookups, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE activity_id = 1 AND instr(',' || '{{bec_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname, answers
config.description: Identify any internal host attempting to resolve the campaign infrastructure.
config.expected_signal: A host resolving these domains suggests a potential victim who clicked a link. Silence proves no resolution occurred via monitored DNS resolvers.

primitive_config.label: DNS lookups for lookalike domains
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, answers, COUNT(*) AS lookups, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE activity_id = 1 AND instr(',' || '{{bec_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname, answers
primitive_config.expected: A host resolving these domains suggests a potential victim who clicked a link. Silence proves no resolution occurred via monitored DNS resolvers.

config.objective: Determine if the DNS lookups for {{bec_domains}} indicate meaningful interaction that should open the gate for connection telemetry.
config.description: Assess the DNS results to decide if the interaction warrants more expensive telemetry searches.
config.expected_signal: A recommendation on whether to proceed with host-level connection analysis.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict on whether the DNS activity is a positive lead for follow-on queries.

config.question: the agent finds at least one host resolving lookalike domains
config.condition: the agent finds at least one host resolving lookalike domains
config.description: Manage query cost by only running parallel telemetry searches if a valid lead exists.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_hostname, process_name, user_name, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE activity_id = 1 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND instr(',' || '{{bec_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify the process and user that connected to the identified infrastructure.
config.expected_signal: A row identifies a browser or application talking to the BEC site. Silence means no established socket was recorded for those domains.

primitive_config.label: Sockets to fraud domains
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_hostname, process_name, user_name, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE activity_id = 1 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND instr(',' || '{{bec_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A row identifies a browser or application talking to the BEC site. Silence means no established socket was recorded for those domains.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, url_hostname, url_full, user_agent, time FROM hb_http_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND instr(',' || '{{bec_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(url_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Inspect the full URL to determine if the user accessed specific invoice or payment portals.
config.expected_signal: Full URI paths show specific interaction targets (e.g., /invoice/ACH). Silence may mean the traffic was encrypted at the proxy.

primitive_config.expected: Full URI paths show specific interaction targets (e.g., /invoice/ACH). Silence may mean the traffic was encrypted at the proxy.

config.objective: Determine if any host successfully engaged with lookalike infrastructure based on the combined telemetry.
config.description: Consolidate DNS, socket, and HTTP results to confirm successful social engineering.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict of malicious | suspicious | benign citing specific process and web activity.
config.success_criteria: A verdict that distinguishes between mere resolution and active session engagement.

config.question: the triage confirms active interaction with fraud infrastructure for at least one host
config.condition: the triage confirms active interaction with fraud infrastructure for at least one host
config.description: Isolate hosts where engagement with the BEC infrastructure is confirmed.
Contain the threat and prevent further fraudulent actions by the user.
config.instructions: Isolate the host and revoke active identity sessions for the involved user account.

config.description: Analyze the extent of the interaction and check for initiated financial transfers.
config.instructions: Review the full URIs in the web-requests step. Check the user inbox for the impersonation emails to verify if they match the AI-generated patterns described in the report. Coordinate with finance to check for pending ACH transfers to unknown bank accounts.
Record all hosts that were examined and found to have no interaction. Add any newly discovered fraudulent IPs to the perimeter blocklist.
